segments.flavor: the Block Radio signature
segments.text: Dez: Block Radio. Respect the craft. Every record in this hour earned its spot. Here comes another one.

segments.flavor: the Block Radio signature
segments.text:
Dez: You are on Block Radio, where nothing gets explained twice.
Dez: [cheerful] You caught it the first time. Let the record run.

segments.flavor: the Block Radio signature
segments.text:
Dez: Block Radio. Two turntables, one standard, no shortcuts.
Dez: If it knocks, it plays. Here it comes.

segments.flavor: the Block Radio signature
segments.text:
Dez: Block Radio. Respect the craft, and the craft respects you back.
Nia: [sarcastic] The craft also hears a clipped snare. Every time.
Dez: She is never wrong. Music.

segments.flavor: Nia breaks down one element of the last beat and lands a verdict
segments.text:
Nia: The kick and the bass were standing in the same doorway.
Dez: Somebody had to move.
Nia: The bass moved. That is why the drop breathes.
Dez: Verdict accepted. Roll the next one.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system that runs the block; Dez gives it one line of respect
segments.text:
Dez: That sound system has run this block since before any of us got here.
Dez: It never asks for credit and it never misses a night. Respect. Music up.

segments.flavor: Walt calls to remember the quiet years and gets corrected with one detail from his own past
segments.text:
Dez: Walt, how was the block back then?
Walt: Quiet. You could hear the ice truck from three streets away.
Nia: Walt, you owned the loudest van on this street.
Walt: [chuckle] That van had taste. Play the record.

segments.flavor: Dez's demo tape comes up again; he says no comment and Nia adds one more fact about it
segments.text:
Nia: I found the paper insert from your demo tape. The tracklist is numbers.
Dez: No comment.
Nia: Track four is called four.
Dez: [sigh] Still no comment. Let the record talk.

segments.flavor: Nia breaks down one element of the last beat and lands a verdict
segments.text:
Dez: Nia, the sample on that one. Talk to me.
Nia: Flute loop, pitched down a whole step, and they left the tape hiss in.
Dez: On purpose?
Nia: [serious] On purpose. That hiss is the glue holding the whole track together.
Dez: That is craft. Keep it rolling.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system that runs the block; Dez gives it one line of respect
segments.text:
Dez: Those corner cabinets were built out of a closet door, two car magnets, and pure stubbornness.
Dez: They still move more air than anything sold with a warranty. Respect. The next record goes through them.

segments.flavor: Walt calls to remember the quiet years and gets corrected with one detail from his own past
segments.text:
Dez: Walt, you said the summers used to be silent around here.
Walt: Silent. A fan in a window and somebody washing a car.
Nia: You had two porch speakers pointed straight at the street.
Walt: [chuckle] They were small speakers, young lady.
Dez: Small and aimed. Take us back in.

segments.flavor: Dez's demo tape comes up again; he says no comment and Nia adds one more fact about it
segments.text:
Nia: Side B of your demo tape is eleven minutes of you counting in.
Dez: No comment.
Nia: Eleven minutes, Dez. One two three four, over and over, with real conviction.
Dez: [sigh] The conviction was free. No comment stands.
Nia: Noted. Let the next record count itself in.

segments.flavor: Nia breaks down one element of the last beat and lands a verdict
segments.text:
Dez: The drums on that last one. What did you hear?
Nia: No swing at all. Every hat sits exactly on the grid.
Dez: And it still knocks.
Nia: It knocks because the handclap lands late. Three frames late, on every four.
Dez: Somebody did that on purpose.
Nia: Somebody did that on purpose for twenty years. Verdict is respect. Run it back.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system that runs the block; Dez gives it one line of respect
segments.text:
Dez: That was the mix, running through the same system that runs this block.
Nia: Whoever owns it replaced the tweeters twice and never touched the tuning.
Dez: Because the tuning was right the first time. That is the whole point.
Nia: [serious] Right the first time is rare. Say that again for the room.
Dez: Right the first time. Respect. Let it ride.

segments.flavor: Walt calls to remember the quiet years and gets corrected with one detail from his own past
segments.text:
Dez: Walt is back. Walt, tell them how peaceful the park used to be.
Walt: Peaceful. Grass, dominoes, and one man selling ice from a cooler.
Nia: [sarcastic] And a drum circle. Every Sunday. Led by you.
Walt: That was community, not noise.
Dez: You had congas and a cowbell, Walt.
Walt: [laugh] The cowbell was borrowed. Play the music, please.

segments.flavor: Dez's demo tape comes up again; he says no comment and Nia adds one more fact about it
segments.text:
Nia: I finally played the whole demo tape through the big speakers in studio two.
Dez: No comment.
Nia: The hook is a cereal jingle. Slowed down, but it is a cereal jingle.
Dez: [groan] No. Comment.
Nia: You even kept the little bell at the end of the jingle.
Dez: That bell was mine. Everything else, no comment. Next one, please.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Dez: Block Radio is brought to you by Bodega Ones canvas sneakers.
Nia: One color. One price. No logo bigger than a thumbnail.
Dez: Bodega Ones. The shoe that looks better after the summer than before it.
Nia: Bodega Ones are not waterproof, not fireproof, and not a personality.
Dez: They are, though. Hit the music.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Nia: RattleStop trunk kits. For the car that knocks and then buzzes.
Dez: Foam, felt, and eight clips. Ten minutes in a parking lot.
Nia: The bass stays. The rattle leaves. Nobody hears the license plate again.
Dez: [cheerful] RattleStop. Because a buzz is not bass.
Nia: RattleStop does not cover mirrors, hubcaps, or arguments with a passenger.
Dez: Back to the music.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Dez: Room Nine is open for rent, by the hour, through the back entrance.
Nia: Concrete floor. Dead corner. A console older than everybody in it.
Dez: Room Nine. No clock on the wall, because the clock is in the headphones.
Nia: The neighbors upstairs work nights, so the room is yours until six.
Dez: Bring your own cables. Bring your own patience.
Nia: Room Nine does not refund a session you slept through.
Dez: Fair enough. Send it back to the record.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Nia: Halfback studio headphones. One cup on, one cup off, the way you actually work.
Dez: The swivel does not squeak. We tested it for an hour.
Nia: [serious] I tested it. He watched.
Dez: Halfback. Hear the room and the mix at the same time.
Nia: Halfback is not responsible for what you miss while listening to yourself.
Dez: [laugh] Take it away.

segments.flavor: Nia breaks down one element of the last beat and lands a verdict
segments.text:
Dez: Nia. The mix on that one. Go.
Nia: The vocal is riding hot and everything else ducks out of its way.
Dez: I noticed the guitar disappearing.
Nia: It does not disappear. It gets pushed down four decibels every time he breathes.
Dez: That is either lazy or genius.
Nia: It is neither. It is a choice, and it makes the voice feel close.
Dez: Verdict?
Nia: The choice works. I would still give the guitar a little room. Let it play.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system that runs the block; Dez gives it one line of respect
segments.text:
Dez: Back through the system that keeps this block honest.
Nia: Honest is the word. That rig has no tricks in it at all.
Dez: No tricks. One box, one horn, and a man who knows exactly where to aim it.
Nia: He aims it at the wall across the street and lets the street do the rest.
Dez: That is engineering.
Nia: That is somebody who listened before he bought anything.
Dez: One line of respect, then we keep it moving.
Nia: Respect. Now let it knock.

segments.flavor: Walt calls to remember the quiet years and gets corrected with one detail from his own past
segments.text:
Dez: Walt called in. Walt, you said the barbershop used to be quiet as a library.
Walt: Quieter. Clippers, a fan, and one man losing at checkers.
Nia: There was a radio behind the third chair. Yours.
Walt: ...that radio was low.
Dez: My uncle said you kept it on the window sill, facing the street.
Walt: [cough] A window sill is not the same as loud.
Nia: The whole corner knew those songs by heart, Walt.
Walt: [chuckle] Fine. That was me. Put something on, and make it something good.

segments.flavor: Dez's demo tape comes up again; he says no comment and Nia adds one more fact about it
segments.text:
Nia: Somebody asked me about the demo tape again.
Dez: No comment.
Nia: I told them the truth. It was recorded in a stairwell for the reverb.
Dez: That stairwell was a good room and it cost nothing.
Nia: There was a choir rehearsing two floors up. They are on the tape.
Dez: [sigh] No comment.
Nia: Track six is you rapping over other people's harmony, and it almost works.
Dez: Almost is generous. That is my only comment. Put a record on.

segments.flavor: Nia breaks down one element of the last beat and lands a verdict
segments.text:
Dez: Break it down for me. That whole beat, one element.
Nia: The drums. It is one break, chopped into eight pieces, and reassembled.
Dez: Sounds like a full kit to me.
Nia: It is not. Listen to the room. The same room tone sits under every hit.
Dez: So the room gives it away.
Nia: The room always gives it away. Somebody recorded that break in a small space.
Dez: And they kept the chop instead of cleaning it.
Nia: They kept the chop because the little stumble at the end makes it swing.
Dez: The mistake is the groove.
Nia: The mistake is always the groove. Verdict is respect, and I want it louder.
Dez: Louder it is. Go.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system that runs the block; Dez gives it one line of respect
segments.text:
Dez: That was the mix, coming back through the loudest honest speakers on this block.
Nia: Honest is right. Nothing boosted. No smile curve. Flat and a little mean.
Dez: The man who runs it sweeps the sidewalk in front of it every morning.
Nia: He sweeps because people stand there. People stand there because it sounds correct.
Dez: I have heard expensive rigs lose to that one.
Nia: Expensive is not the same as tuned. It never has been.
Dez: Same two horns for thirty years. New grill cloth every spring.
Nia: That is the whole secret. Somebody keeps it alive and never once brags.
Dez: Respect to the corner. Send the music back through it.

segments.flavor: Walt calls to remember the quiet years and gets corrected with one detail from his own past
segments.text:
Dez: Walt is on the line and he has a complaint. Walt.
Walt: Everything is loud now. When I came up, this block went to sleep at ten.
Nia: Walt. The block party.
Walt: What block party?
Nia: The one with the generator, two speakers, and an extension cord across the street.
Dez: Somebody told me it ran until sunrise. Twice.
Walt: ...it ran until sunrise once.
Nia: And the second night?
Walt: [cough] The second night the generator quit. That is not the same thing.
Dez: [laugh] So the block was quiet because the gas ran out.
Walt: The block was quiet because we were tired. Put the music on, young man.
Dez: Gladly. Here it goes.

segments.flavor: Dez's demo tape comes up again; he says no comment and Nia adds one more fact about it
segments.text:
Nia: I digitized the whole demo tape this week. Both sides, all forty minutes.
Dez: No comment.
Nia: The bass is only on the left side. The entire tape, start to finish.
Dez: ...no comment.
Nia: You mixed the whole thing on headphones with one dead cup, did you not?
Dez: [sigh] The right cup worked fine.
Nia: The right cup had no bass in it, Dez. You could not hear what you were doing.
Dez: I could hear the hook, and the hook is what matters.
Nia: The hook is good. It is genuinely good. I will say that once and never again.
Dez: [surprised] Wait. Say that again.
Nia: No. Once. Now play the record and let it go.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Dez: The Brickbox Four Hundred has arrived, and it does one thing.
Nia: Sixteen pads. One knob. No screen, no menu, no updates ever.
Dez: You load your sounds, you hit the pads, you keep the take.
Nia: The knob is volume. That is the only knob it will ever be.
Dez: Brickbox. Built in a shop, not in a boardroom.
Nia: Brickbox is not responsible for beats made at four in the morning.
Dez: Nobody ever is. Music, please.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Nia: The Dig Bag holds fifty records and one sandwich.
Dez: Canvas body. Real leather strap. A seam that has never once let go.
Nia: Fifty records is heavy. The strap knows. The strap does not care.
Dez: Dig Bag. Made for people who walk home with the whole crate.
Nia: Dig Bag is not liable for warped records, sore shoulders, or empty wallets.
Dez: Worth it. Back to the block.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Dez: The Kitchen Table Mic is for the closet booth and the coat rack.
Nia: One capsule. One pattern. It hears the voice and ignores the refrigerator.
Dez: No shock mount needed. Hang it from anything that does not move.
Nia: [serious] Anything that does not move. That part is the whole instruction.
Dez: The Kitchen Table Mic. Because the room is the problem, not the money.
Nia: It will not fix your neighbors, your ceiling, or your writing.
Dez: Two out of three would be nice. Music, go.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sneakers, car speakers or a studio for rent, rapid disclaimer from Nia
segments.text:
Nia: Storm Door Company. They build a door that actually closes.
Dez: Ours does not. Ours has never closed in its entire life.
Nia: One hinge, one sweep, one latch that catches the first time.
Dez: Storm Door. Peace of mind, measured in decibels.
Nia: Storm Door cannot remove a cousin who is already in the hallway.
Dez: [laugh] Nothing can. Open the faders.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — Craft Check
segments.text:
Dez: Craft Check. One rule, one test, every time.
Nia: The rule is the small speaker rule.
Dez: If a beat only works on a big system, it does not work.
Nia: Play it on a phone. Play it in a kitchen. Play it on a laptop.
Dez: If the kick vanishes, the kick was never really there.
Nia: The low end you feel is not the low end you hear. Build for both.
Dez: That is Craft Check. Play something loud.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — House Rules
segments.text:
Nia: House rule number four. Nobody touches the faders but me.
Dez: House rule number five. Nobody sits on the couch during a take.
Nia: That couch squeaks. It has squeaked through three good verses.
Dez: Four good verses.
Nia: [sigh] Four. And the couch stays, because everyone likes the couch.
Dez: Rule number six. If you break a rule, you buy the coffee.
Nia: Somebody owes me a lot of coffee.
Dez: I do not know who that could be. Start the record.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — Sample Court
segments.text:
Dez: Sample Court is in session. Nia, the charge.
Nia: The charge is laziness. Two bars looped, nothing moved, nothing added.
Dez: The defense?
Nia: The defense is that the two bars are perfect and they knew it.
Dez: Did they filter it?
Nia: They filtered the top off in the second verse. That is one small effort.
Dez: One effort is not a defense.
Nia: It is if the loop carries the whole record. And this one does.
Dez: Then the court finds the flip honest. Case closed.
Nia: Honest, not lazy. There is a difference and it is audible.
Dez: Court adjourned. Put the record back on.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — One Knob
segments.text:
Nia: One Knob. If they took every control off that board but one.
Dez: I keep the high pass. Everything gets cleaner the second you use it.
Nia: Wrong. You keep the fader.
Dez: The fader is not a knob.
Nia: The fader is the only knob that matters. Loud and quiet is the whole job.
Dez: [chuckle] She wins this one. She wins most of them.
Nia: One Knob, settled. Let the music up.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — First Bar
segments.text:
Dez: First Bar. A record gets one bar to earn the rest of itself.
Nia: Some records need two. I allow two.
Dez: Generous. The last one earned it in four beats.
Nia: It earned it in the first hit. That snare arrives before you are ready.
Dez: Early snare, late clap. Somebody in there knows exactly what they are doing.
Nia: Nobody accidentally builds a first bar like that.
Dez: That is First Bar. The rest of the record is homework.
Nia: And it did the homework. Roll it back in.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — Dollar Bin
segments.text:
Nia: Dollar Bin. One record, no label, no name on it anywhere.
Dez: Bought for a dollar out of a milk crate on a folding table.
Nia: Play the intro. Eleven seconds of organ and a woman clearing her throat.
Dez: Then the drums come in and the whole thing sounds like a church basement.
Nia: Because it was one. Somebody's uncle owned that organ.
Dez: Somebody pressed a hundred of these and gave them all to family.
Nia: And one of them survived a milk crate. That is the whole story.
Dez: Dollar Bin. Cheapest lesson in the building. Drop the needle.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — Two Words
segments.text:
Dez: Two Words. Nia reviews the last record in exactly two words.
Nia: Patient. Expensive.
Dez: Expensive?
Nia: Somebody paid for that string section. Nobody fakes those bows.
Dez: Two words, and I have four follow-up questions.
Nia: You get none. That is the point of the bit.
Dez: [laugh] Hard rules on this show. Bring the music back.

segments.flavor: recurring bit — The Ending
segments.text:
Dez: Nobody talks about the last bar. Everybody talks about the first one.
Nia: The ending tells you whether anyone was still paying attention.
Dez: A fade is a shrug.
Nia: A fade is a shrug. A hard stop is a decision.
Dez: That one stopped dead on the four. No reverb tail, nothing.
Nia: It stopped because the song was finished. That is rare and I respect it.
Dez: Learn the ending, and the beginning takes care of itself.
Nia: Now let the next one start properly.
